display_title: TechBridge: Oproep Duitsland 2026 – Next-Generation Battery Technologies and Manufacturing – TechBridge
organization_or_parent_framework: Ministerie van Economische Zaken en Klimaat
call_title: TechBridge: Oproep Duitsland 2026 – Next-Generation Battery Technologies and Manufacturing
executive_summary: Bilateral German-Dutch TechBridge call, run by RVO for the Dutch side under title 3.8 (Internationaal innoveren) of the Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies and funded from the National Growth Fund project Material Independence and Circular Batteries, for joint R&D on next-generation battery cell materials and cell manufacturing (TRL 4 to 7) aimed at niche markets such as aviation, drones, heavy-duty applications and robotics. Consortia need at least one company from Germany and one from the Netherlands; the Dutch side must be led by a for-profit Dutch company, and knowledge institutions may join. RVO grants up to EUR 2 million per Dutch consortium (total Dutch budget EUR 2 million) at 25% to 50% of R&D costs depending on organisation type and research or development work. Applications are due on 19 January 2027, 17:00 CET; projects start from 1 June 2027 and last at most 36 months.
status_rationale: The call text (sections 2 and 3) funds next-generation battery cell materials, cell assembly and manufacturing equipment concepts, with cell-level energy-density and cycle-life targets, for niche markets such as aviation, drones, heavy-duty applications and robotics, and says mass markets are not targeted. It does not touch TenneT's field: it covers no stationary storage, grid connection or flexibility use, and no project file is close; the only link, better cells for the drones used in Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM), is too remote from the call's cell-chemistry scope. The project end date was derived from the earliest start of 1 June 2027 and the maximum duration of 36 months.
